texts.li: {A_nameDef} has been woken every night this week by people coming in and going out past {A_possessive} bed, which stands nearest the door. {B_nameDef}'s bed is at the far wall, where nobody passes, and {B_nameDef} sleeps like a stone wherever {B_pronoun} lies.

{A_nameDef} came to the council grey with lost sleep. The bed {A_pronoun} sleeps in is the first one by the door, and the door is never still at night. {A_pronoun} would like to change places with {B_nameDef}, at the quiet end, if the council will put it to {B_objective}.

[lowtech] {A_nameDef} sleeps by the door of the long hut, and every time someone goes out to the fire or comes back from it, {A_pronoun} is awake again. {B_nameDef}, at the far end, never hears a thing.

li.label: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} trade beds
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} took the bed by the door without much complaint, and {A_nameDef} has the one at the far wall from tonight.

li.label: {A_nameDef} sleeps late tomorrow
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is to sleep late tomorrow and start work when {A_pronoun} wakes. The others have been asked to come in quietly.

li.label: A shared room is a shared room
li.outcome: The council said a shared room is a shared room, and {A_nameDef} went back to it.

li.label: a quiet bed at last
li.description: I sleep at the far wall now, where nobody walks past at night. I slept right through.

li.label: moved to the bed by the door
li.description: The council gave my quiet bed away and put me by the door. I can sleep anywhere, but still.

li.label: allowed a morning's sleep
li.description: The council let me sleep late to make up for the bad nights. It helped.

li.label: woken every night
li.description: I asked the council about the bed by the door, and nothing changed. I still wake every time someone comes in.

texts.li: {PET_nameDef} died yesterday, and {A_nameDef} has hardly left the body since. {A_pronoun} asks that {PET_nameDef} be laid in one of the colony's graves, with the colony's own dead. {B_nameDef} says the colony's graves are for its people.

{A_nameDef} sat beside {PET_nameDef} most of the night. In the morning {A_pronoun} came to the council and asked for one of the empty graves. {B_nameDef} thinks a grave is a lot to give an animal, and has said so.

[lowtech] {PET_nameDef} slept at {A_nameDef}'s feet by the fire for years and followed {A_objective} everywhere by day. Now {A_nameDef} asks for a place for {PET_objective} in the ground where the colony lays its own. {B_nameDef} says the ground is for people.

li.label: {PET_nameDef} has the empty grave
li.outcome: The empty grave is given to {PET_nameDef}, who will be laid in it as the colony's own dead are.

li.label: An hour beside {PET_nameDef}, and then the usual way
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sat beside {PET_nameDef} a while, with one other for company. After that, {PET_nameDef} goes where the colony's dead animals go.

lines.li: You were a good animal, the best.
Rest now, you've done enough.

li.label: An animal is an animal
li.outcome: The council said no to it. {A_nameDef} took that quietly.

li.label: a grave for my animal
li.description: My animal has a grave of its own, with the colony's dead. I'm grateful to the council for that.

li.label: a grave given to an animal
li.description: The council gave one of our graves to an animal. I don't think that was right.

li.label: sat with my animal a while
li.description: I sat with my animal for an hour before it was taken away. I'm glad I had that.

li.label: no grave for my animal
li.description: I asked for a grave for my animal and the council said no. It was with me for years.

texts.li: The stores have been stacked with {THING} since the insects were killed, {COUNT} meals of it at least. {A_nameDef}, who does the cooking, says meat is meat and the colony can't afford to waste it. {B_nameDef} says nobody will eat it knowing what it is.

There is more {THING} in the cold store than anything else, and it does not smell like other meat. {A_nameDef} would cook it into the meals and say nothing. {B_nameDef} would rather the animals had it.
[lowtech] The insects are dead and their meat is piled by the fire pit, pale and waxy. {A_nameDef} says the colony has eaten worse in hard winters. {B_nameDef} doubts that very much.

li.label: Cook it into the meals
li.outcome: The {THING} is to be cooked into simple meals, with nothing else in them. Those who eat them will know what is in them, but the meat will not go to waste.

li.label: Kibble for the animals
li.outcome: The {THING} goes into kibble for the colony's animals, with plant food to make up the rest.

li.label: Keep it for a hungry day
li.outcome: The {THING} stays where it is, kept for a day when there is nothing else.

li.label: insect meat in the meals
li.description: The council decided we'll be eating insect meat in our meals. I'd rather not think about it.

li.label: good meat for the animals
li.description: That meat could have fed people. Now it's going to the animals.

li.label: food left lying in the stores
li.description: All that meat is just sitting in the stores. Nobody wants to decide what to do with it.

texts.li: The wild fruit is ripe all round the colony, more of it than anyone can remember. {A_nameDef} asks for a day when everyone goes out together to pick it, the way it was done where {A_pronoun} grew up, and nobody minds the stains.
{A_nameDef} came back from beyond the fields with purple hands and a full hat. There is more out there, {A_pronoun} says, enough for everyone, if the colony would give it a morning.
[land:desert] The agave is ripe on the slopes round the colony. {A_nameDef} asks for a day when everyone goes out to cut it together, before the heat and the animals get to it first.
[lowtech] In {A_nameDef}'s old village the young and the old went out together when the wild fruit was ripe, and came home singing. {A_nameDef} would like a day like that here.
[again] The wild fruit is ripe again, and {A_nameDef} has the baskets out by the door. Last summer's picking day was a good one, {A_pronoun} says, and this one should be the same.
[tradition] The picking day comes round with the ripe fruit now. {A_nameDef} has the baskets ready and wants only the council's word.

li.label: Everyone out to pick
li.outcome: The colony went out together and picked what was ripe within reach, wild and sown, and carried it in to the stores before the afternoon was out.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] They went out together with baskets and carried the wild fruit back on their hips, and {A_nameDef} was last in with the fullest basket.
[tradition] The picking day went as it always does: everyone out from morning, the baskets carried in, and {A_nameDef} last back with stained hands.

lines.li: There's more over by the rocks, bring the basket.
One for the basket and one for me.
Mind the thorns on that side.

li.label: A morning of it, for those who can be spared
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and a few others spent the morning picking what grew wild near the colony, and carried it in.

li.label: The work comes first
li.outcome: The council said the work comes first. The wild fruit is left to whoever finds it.

li.label: the picking day
li.description: We all went out together to pick the wild fruit. My hands are still stained, and I don't mind.

texts.li: There are about {COUNT} days of food left, and the new crops are a long way off. {A_nameDef}, who does the cooking, asks who is to come first when the pot runs short: the children, the old and the ill, or those at the hardest work. {B_nameDef} says the ones who bring the food in can't do it hungry.

[winter] The stores are down to about {COUNT} days of food and the snow is still on the fields. {A_nameDef} says it's time the colony decided who comes first at the pot, before it has to decide in a hurry.

[lowtech] The pots are getting thinner, and {A_nameDef}, who keeps them, asks the council: the little ones, the old and the sick first, as {A_possessive} people always did, or the ones who dig and haul? {B_nameDef} has an answer, and it is the second.

li.label: Those who need it most come first
li.outcome: This evening those who need it most sat down to eat first, before anyone else.

li.label: supper for those who need it most
Those at the hardest work come first
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} took meals out to those working in the open, so that they could eat at the work.

li.label: meals carried out to the workers

lines.li: Here, eat this before you go back to it.
It's not much, but it's hot.

li.label: No one goes before anyone else
li.outcome: The council said no one goes before anyone else, and the pot is shared as it always was.

li.label: the workers come last
li.description: I work the hardest of anyone, and I'm to eat after the others. I understand why, but my stomach doesn't.

li.label: fed first, at the work
li.description: The council put the ones at the hard work first. Someone brought a meal out to us.

li.label: the pot shared alike
li.description: Food is short, but nobody here goes before anybody else. That seems fair to me.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} and {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} have been talking every chance they get since the visitors arrived. {A_nameDef} would like to see {X_objective} off properly, with something from the colony's stores for the road. {B_nameDef} says the stores are not for every visitor who is friendly.

{X_nameDef} came with the {FACTION} party and has spent more time at {A_nameDef}'s side than with {X_possessive} own people. Before they go, {A_nameDef} wants to give {X_objective} something to remember the colony by. {B_nameDef} would rather {A_nameDef} got on with {A_possessive} work.

[theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has sat with {A_nameDef} at the fire every evening of the visit, the two of them trading stories. {A_nameDef} asks the council's leave to send {X_objective} on with food for the road.

li.label: {A_nameDef} takes {X_nameDef} food for the road
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} took two meals from the stores out to {X_nameDef}, who put them away in {X_possessive} pack for the road.

li.label: An hour together before the visitors go
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} went to find {X_nameDef}, and the two of them talked for an hour.

li.label: Guests come and go
li.outcome: The council said guests come and go. {A_nameDef} went back to work.

li.label: saw a friend off
li.description: I made a friend among the visitors and got to see them off properly. I hope they come this way again.

li.label: no proper goodbye
li.description: I made a friend among the visitors, and the council wouldn't give me the time to see them off.

texts.li: The songs of {NAME} are being sung all over the region, and one of them is about the colony. {A_nameDef} says the colony ought to have a verse of its own to answer it, made up by its own people round the fire. {B_nameDef} says the colony has better things to do with an evening than rhyme.

{A_nameDef} has been trying out lines under {A_possessive} breath all week, and has asked {B_nameDef} to help with the rest. If the colony is going to be sung about by {NAME}, {A_pronoun} says, it might as well have a say in it.

[lowtech] Every traveller who passes is humming one of the tunes of {NAME}. {A_nameDef} would have the colony sit round the fire one night and make a song of its own, about the people here and what they have lived through.

li.label: An evening at the fire to make the verse
li.outcome: The colony sat round the fire that evening and made up a verse of its own, a line from whoever had one, and sang it through before bed.

lines.li: Here's a line for the verse, see if it fits.
Sing that last part again, slower this time.
Put in the winter we nearly ran out of food.
It doesn't rhyme, but leave it in.
All together on the last line now.

li.label: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} work it out between them
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} sat down at the table one evening and worked out a verse between them.

li.label: Leave the verses to {NAME}
li.outcome: The council said the verses can be left to {NAME}.

li.label: a verse of our own
li.description: We made a verse about this place ourselves. It isn't good, but it's ours.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} called {B_nameDef} by the wrong name twice yesterday, and stood a long time in the storeroom this morning without knowing what {A_pronoun} had come for. {A_pronoun} is still at {WORK} every day and will not hear of stopping. {B_nameDef} has come to the council, gently, about what is to be done.

{A_nameDef} is forgetting things, more of them every season: names, the way to the stores, what {A_pronoun} said an hour ago. {A_pronoun} is still at {WORK} for the colony, and does it well enough most days. {B_nameDef} asks the council what should be done before something goes wrong.

[lowtech] The old ones say the mind goes before the body in some people, and it has started to go in {A_nameDef}. {B_nameDef}, who sits nearest {A_objective} at the fire, has asked the council what can be done, and whether {A_nameDef} should keep on at {WORK}.

li.label: {B_nameDef} sits down with {A_nameDef} and goes over the names
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} sat down with {A_nameDef} that evening and went through the colony's people one by one, and how each of them came to be here.

li.label: {B_nameDef} takes {A_nameDef}'s place at {WORK} for a season
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} takes {A_nameDef}'s place at {WORK} for a season, and {A_nameDef} took it well enough.

li.label: {A_nameDef} keeps on as before
li.outcome: The council will not take {A_nameDef}'s work from {A_objective} while {A_pronoun} can still do it.

li.label: the names gone over
li.description: Someone sat with me and went over everyone's names, and how they came here. I'll forget again, but it was good to hear.

li.label: my work given to another
li.description: They've given my work to someone else for a while. I know why. I don't have to like it.

li.label: still trusted with my work
li.description: The council let me keep my work. I can still do it, whatever people say.

li.label: worried about a friend
li.description: My friend is forgetting things and still at the work as if nothing were wrong. I worry about it.

texts.li: {THIRD_nameDef} has been crying half the night, every night, and {A_nameDef} has been up with {THIRD_objective} through all of it. {A_pronoun} fell asleep over {A_possessive} bowl at breakfast. {B_nameDef} has offered to take a turn with the little one, if the council agrees.

{A_nameDef} has the look of someone who has not slept properly in a week, because {A_pronoun} hasn't: {THIRD_nameDef} is hungry, or uncomfortable, or simply small, and cries until someone comes. {B_nameDef} says it is somebody else's turn.
[lowtech] The little one, {THIRD_nameDef}, cries in the dark, and {A_nameDef} is always the one who gets up. The others hear it too. {B_nameDef} has said {B_pronoun} will take a turn.

li.label: {B_nameDef} sees to {THIRD_nameDef} for a few days
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} takes over seeing to {THIRD_nameDef} for a few days, and {A_nameDef} gets {A_possessive} nights back.

li.label: {A_nameDef} sleeps this afternoon
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} was sent to bed for the afternoon, to make up some of the sleep.

li.label: Babies cry
li.outcome: The council said babies cry, and someone has to get up for them. {A_nameDef} went back to it.

li.label: someone else up with the little one
li.description: Someone else is getting up with the little one for a while. I slept a whole night.

li.label: an afternoon's sleep
li.description: They sent me to bed for the afternoon. I needed it more than I let on.

li.label: up again with the little one
li.description: I asked for help with the nights and the council said babies cry. I know they do.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} lost {A_possessive} temper the other day and broke what was nearest. {A_pronoun} is calm again now, and a little ashamed. {B_nameDef} wants the council to say whether {A_nameDef} mends the damage, says sorry in front of everyone, or whether it is to be forgotten.
Everyone heard it: {A_nameDef} smashing things in a rage that went on for most of an afternoon. Now there is mending to be done round the colony, and {B_nameDef} asks whose job it is.

[lowtech] When the rage took {A_nameDef}, {A_pronoun} kicked and broke whatever was near. {B_nameDef} says that among {B_possessive} people the one who breaks a thing mends it, and asks the council to say the same.

li.label: {A_nameDef} mends the damage
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} spent a few hours mending what needed mending round the colony, and cleaning up after.

li.label: {A_nameDef} says sorry at supper
li.outcome: At supper {A_nameDef} stood up and said sorry to everyone for the damage and the noise. It was short, and nobody made it harder.

lines.li: I'm sorry for what I broke, and for the shouting.
I lost my temper and I'm ashamed of it.
It won't happen again if I can help it.

li.label: A bad day, and no more
li.outcome: The council said it was a bad day and let it go. {B_nameDef} did not think much of that.

li.label: mended what I broke
li.description: I spent the day putting right what I broke. I feel better for it.

li.label: it was put right
li.description: Whoever breaks something should put it right, and the council saw to it that they did.

li.label: said sorry in front of everyone
li.description: I said sorry to everyone at supper. It was hard to say, and better once it was said.

li.label: let off
li.description: The council let my bad day go. I'll try to deserve that.

li.label: nothing done about it
li.description: Someone broke half the place in a rage and the council called it a bad day.

texts.li: {DEAD} never had any time for the gods and said so, often, at supper. Now {DEAD} is in the ground, and {A_nameDef} would go to the grave at dusk and say {GOD}'s words over it all the same. {B_nameDef}, who was {DEAD}'s friend, says {DEAD} would have hated it.

{A_nameDef} holds to {GOD}, and says nobody should go into the ground without the words said. {DEAD}, who lies there now, laughed at the words while living. {B_nameDef} would say something plainer at the grave, in {DEAD}'s own way, or nothing at all.

[lowtech] Among {A_nameDef}'s people the dead are given to {GOD} with the old words, whatever they believed. {DEAD} believed in nothing but the fire and the next meal, {B_nameDef} says, and should be let be.

li.label: {A_nameDef} says {GOD}'s words at the grave
li.outcome: At dusk {A_nameDef} stood at {DEAD}'s grave and said {GOD}'s words over it, with whoever came.

lines.li: Rest thee now, whatever thou didst believe.
Into the ground thou goest, and the words go with thee.

li.label: {B_nameDef} says a few plain words
li.outcome: At dusk {B_nameDef} said a few plain words at {DEAD}'s grave, the way {DEAD} would have liked: who {DEAD} was, and what {DEAD} did here.

lines.li: {DEAD} worked as hard as anyone here and never made a fuss about it.
{DEAD} would laugh at us all standing here like this.
We'll miss {DEAD} at the table, I know I will.

li.label: Nothing said, as {DEAD} would have wanted
li.outcome: The council would have nothing said over {DEAD}, and it was left at that.

li.label: said the words over the dead
li.description: I said the words over the grave. Whatever they believed, they deserved that much.

li.label: words my friend would have hated
li.description: They said a god's words over my friend's grave. My friend laughed at all of that.

li.label: said a few words for my friend
li.description: I said a few plain words at my friend's grave, the kind they would have liked.

li.label: no holy words at the grave
li.description: Someone went into the ground without the words said over them. It doesn't sit right with me.

li.label: my friend left in peace
li.description: Nobody said a god's words over my friend. They would have been glad of that.

texts.li: {A_nameDef}'s faith forbids meat, and twice this week there was nothing else in the stores. {A_nameDef} ate it, and has not been right since. {A_pronoun} asks that the kitchen keep a pot without meat for those of the colony who hold to the same faith. {B_nameDef}, who does the cooking, says one pot is work enough.

The faith {A_nameDef} holds to will not have meat, and the colony's meals are full of it. {A_nameDef} went hungry for a day, and then ate what there was. {B_nameDef} could cook a pot without meat beside the other, if the council asks it.

[lowtech] There has been nothing but meat over the cooking fire for days, and {A_nameDef}, whose faith forbids it, has been eating it with {A_possessive} eyes shut. {B_nameDef} keeps the fire, and has been asked for a pot without.

li.label: A pot without meat for the faithful
li.outcome: Meals without meat go first on the stove, enough for the faithful for a while.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] A pot without meat goes over the fire first, enough for the faithful for a while.

li.label: {A_nameDef} learns the stove at {B_nameDef}'s side
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} spent the afternoon at {B_nameDef}'s side, learning to cook, so that the faithful can see to their own pot.

li.label: The colony's pot is the colony's pot
li.outcome: The council said there is one pot for the whole colony.

li.label: a pot without meat
li.description: The kitchen keeps a pot without meat for those of my faith now. I won't have to choose between going hungry and going against it.

li.label: learning to cook my own
li.description: I spent the afternoon learning the stove, so I can cook what my faith allows.

li.label: one pot, and it's meat
li.description: The council said there is one pot for everyone, and the pot is full of meat my faith forbids.
